chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan al-Lu'lu'i, who raised it from Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A worshipper prayed to Allah for eighty years. Then he fell in love with a woman and fulfilled his desires with her. When the angel of death approached him, he became mute. A beggar happened to pass by. That person pointed out the beggar to take the piece of bread lying in his pocket. The Almighty Allah had destroyed his worship of eighty years due to the adultery committed by him but He forgave him for offering that piece of bread.

key_terms.فَوَقَعَتْ فِی نَفْسِهِ: it fell in his heart/mind (he fell in love)

ai.seo_question: How can a single act of charity compensate for decades of worship lost to a major sin?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narrative to illustrate the profound impact of a single decisive act of charity (Sadaqah) in offsetting major sins, even for those with extensive devotional histories. The story highlights the concept of 'Habt al-'amal' (nullification of deeds) due to sin, yet demonstrates that sincere, spontaneous charity can serve as a powerful expiation, securing divine forgiveness despite the gravity of the transgression.
